bull.b: Low-20s constant-currency sales guidance alongside at least 65% gross margin and 19.5%-20% adjusted EBITDA margin indicates management expects growth to coexist with strong economics. If delivered, this supports reinvestment, resilience, and durable earnings expansion rather than growth dependent on sacrificing profitability.

Rapid DTC growth and a rising share of sales give On greater control over presentation, customer relationships and channel mix. Continued expansion through owned digital and retail channels can support brand equity and profitability while reducing reliance on third-party distribution over the medium term.

Strong apparel and training growth shows On is extending beyond its core running-shoe franchise, while ongoing technology launches create additional reasons to buy. Broader categories and differentiated products can increase customer lifetime value, diversify revenue, and sustain brand relevance.

bear.b: Deliberately reducing wholesale sell-in protects full-price positioning but creates a near-term constraint on reported revenue and makes growth more dependent on DTC execution. The resulting cadence shift could weigh on operating leverage and complicate channel planning during the next several quarters.

A roughly 30% inventory increase raises the importance of accurate demand planning as wholesale orders are recalibrated. If sell-through does not keep pace, On could require more promotions or carry working capital longer, potentially pressuring margins and cash conversion.

Higher U.S. import tariffs create an external cost burden that can pressure gross margin or require price and sourcing responses. Because expected refunds depend on timing and were excluded from current results and guidance, the near-term earnings and cash benefit remains uncertain.
